sources.articleTitle: Kenya discharges last patient, begins countdown to Ebola-free status
Kenya begins 42-day countdown towards Ebola-free status after discharging last patient

headline: Kenya Commences Final Countdown To Attain Official Ebola-Free Status
seoTitle: Kenya Begins Final Countdown to Ebola-Free Status
metaDescription: Kenya has started a 42-day observation period after discharging its final Ebola patient, targeting an official disease-free declaration by late December.
aiSummaryBullets: Health authorities have released the country's final patient diagnosed with the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola.
A total of 11 individuals who were under close observation as contacts have now been cleared from monitoring.
The nation must remain free of new recorded cases for 42 days to be formally recognized as Ebola-free by health agencies.
aiContextParagraph: Following the discharge of the final patient, Kenya has entered a critical monitoring phase to verify the containment of the Ebola virus. Health officials confirmed that all identified contacts linked to the most recent cases have successfully completed their observation period without developing symptoms of the disease. The current 42-day window is a standard epidemiological requirement to ensure the virus is no longer circulating within the population. If no additional infections are reported, the government expects to achieve an official Ebola-free status on December 23, 2026. This process marks a significant step in the public health efforts to curb the spread of the Bundibugyo strain, which had prompted earlier surveillance and contact tracing protocols across the country. Authorities remain vigilant during this final phase of the containment operation to ensure the safety of the public and verify the eradication of the recent outbreak.
whyItIsViral: The report has gained visibility across primary domestic media outlets as the nation nears a major health milestone, reflected in a moderate viral activity score.
